metadata.title: How to Cook Rice | Indian Style Rice Recipe by Manjula Kitchen
metadata.description:
How to Cook Rice | Indian Style Rice Recipe by Manjula Kitchen

View full recipe at https://manjulaskitchen.com/rice-plain-white/ 

Ingredients: 
• 1 cup Basmati rice or long grain rice 
• 2 cups water 
• 1/2 teaspoon salt 
• 1 teaspoon oil

View More Rice Recipes:
https://youtu.be/26NMjTvr5UA?si=2V7n0yQudbAKOVb_
https://youtu.be/XWSIu8CebZY?si=UJ0-hkkuDtyoq9Q-



If you love Indian vegetarian cooking, check out my Ebook of delicious recipes on Amazon by Manjula.  https://manjulaskitchen.com/manjulas-kitchen-e-book-best-of-indian-vegetarian-recipes/

transcript.text: Today I will be making rice or chawal.
There is variety of rice and everybody has there favorites.
I like the basmati rice, they smell and taste.
Rice is very simple to make.
Plain rice usually served with dal
or any gravy based dish.
This recipe will serve 3-4 people.
I have 1 cup of basmati rice.
2 cups of water
1 tablespoon of oil
1/2 teaspoon of salt
You wash the rice changing the water several times.
And soak at least for 15 minutes.
Here I already have the rice which I have soaked
about half an hour back.
Heat is on, medium high.
I have 2 cups of water.
Oil
Salt
And rice.
So let the rice come to boil before we will cover the rice
and make the heat to low.
And you don't stir the rice in between till it's almost ready.
If you have too much water
rice will become kind of mushy.
Or if you have less water they will be hard.
Or if you have cooked the rice on high heat
the grains will be not soft enough.
Water is boiling.
So I will lower the heat to low.
And cover the pan.
And I will check it after 12 minutes.
And don't stir the rice
like I said otherwise you are going to make the rice mushy.
Rice has been cooking for about 12 minutes.
It's time to check.
And I will check it lightly with a fork
without breaking any grains.
So it needs to cook still for about 3 more minutes.
It has little water and grains are still little hard.
It has been about 4-5 minutes.
So let's check the rice.
They look really good.
And like I said basmati rice they really smell good.
I am just going to check the grain.
And it's soft and tender.
Rice is easy to cook.
But you have to make sure you don't stir much
too many times while rice is cooking.
Rice is easy dish to cook.
It smells good.
I really like the smell of basmati rice.
As you see rice has expanded to about 3 times in the volume
what we started with.
So make sure your pot is large enough.
Today I am going to serve the rice with moong dal
and vegetable kofta.
I will see you again with a new recipe.
Thank you.

nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a lady making a rice dish in a clear bowl in a kitchen. She sets up the bowl on the counter, begins to heat the water in a pot on the stovetop, adds the rice and covers it with a glass lid, checks the water, opens the lid, and removes the rice. Then, she uses a spatula to scoop out the rice and places it into a white plate for display.

The video is a tutorial, and the kitchen setting is bright. The focus is on the rice preparation.

summary.brief: Manjula rinses, cooks, and plates plain basmati rice on the stovetop.
summary.detailed: The video begins with Manjula standing at a kitchen counter showing the measured ingredients—basmati rice, water, oil, and salt. She rinses the rice in a bowl, changing the water several times, and lets it soak for about fifteen minutes. She places a pot on the stove, adds the water, a splash of oil, and the salt, and brings the mixture to a boil. When it boils, she adds the soaked rice, allows it to return to a boil, then lowers the heat and covers the pot with a glass lid. She lets the rice simmer without stirring, checking its doneness after roughly twelve minutes by gently probing with a fork. When the grains are soft and fluffy, she lifts the lid, fluffs the rice with a spatula, and transfers the cooked rice onto a white serving plate. The video ends with her holding the plated rice and addressing the camera.

action.detailed: Heat water with oil and salt, add the soaked basmati rice, bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer without stirring, check for tenderness, then fluff and transfer the rice to a plate.
action.actor: Manjula, the woman in a traditional sari presenting the recipe

summary.brief: A woman prepares basmati rice on the stove, simmering it covered and then fluffing and serving it.
summary.detailed: She measures one cup of basmati rice, rinses it several times and soaks it for about fifteen minutes. She then adds the soaked rice, two cups of water, a tablespoon of oil and half a teaspoon of salt to a pot on a medium‑high flame and brings the mixture to a boil. summary_sent_to_llm.title: How to Cook Rice | Indian Style Rice Recipe by Manjula Kitchen
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
How to Cook Rice | Indian Style Rice Recipe by Manjula Kitchen

View full recipe at https://manjulaskitchen.com/rice-plain-white/ 

Ingredients: 
• 1 cup Basmati rice or long grain rice 
• 2 cups water 
• 1/2 teaspoon salt 
• 1 teaspoon oil

View More Rice Recipes:
https://youtu.be/26NMjTvr5UA?si=2V7n0yQudbAKOVb_
https://youtu.be/XWSIu8CebZY?si=UJ0-hkkuDtyoq9Q-



If you love Indian vegetarian cooking, check out my Ebook of delicious recipes on Amazon by Manjula.  https://manjulaskitchen.com/manjulas-kitchen-e-book-best-of-indian-vegetarian-recipes/ 


Host: Manjula
Copyright: Manjula’s Kitche
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video begins with Manjula standing at a kitchen counter showing the measured ingredients—basmati rice, water, oil, and salt. She rinses the rice in a bowl, changing the water several times, and lets it soak for about fifteen minutes. She places a pot on the stove, adds the water, a splash of oil, and the salt, and brings the mixture to a boil. When it boils, she adds the soaked rice, allows it to return to a boil, then lowers the heat and covers the pot with a glass lid. She lets the rice simmer without stirring, checking its doneness after roughly twelve minutes by gently probing with a fork. When the grains are soft and fluffy, she lifts the lid, fluffs the rice with a spatula, and transfers the cooked rice onto a white serving plate. The video ends with her holding the plated rice and addressing the camera.
action_list: Combine rice with water, oil, and salt
Add oil, salt, and rice to pot

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
